design.source: Raman et al., Nature 515, 540-544 (2014), Fig. 1d, top to bottom on 200 nm Ag

conditions.sun: ASTM G173 AM1.5 global, normal incidence

layer_thickness_provenance: Confirmed from Raman et al., Nature 515, 540-544 (2014), Fig. 1d diagram and text: 7 alternating layers of SiO2 (230, 688, 73, 54 nm) and HfO2 (485, 13, 34 nm) on 200 nm Ag.

gap_analysis.explanation: The 28.3 W/m² gap between simulated 11.8 W/m² and published 40.1 W/m² is predominantly thermal, not solar. Because solar reflectance is 97.7%, reducing solar irradiance from 1000 W/m² (normal AM1.5) to 850 W/m² (tilted rooftop in paper) accounts for only +3.45 W/m². Even in complete darkness (P_sun = 0), simulated P_net is 34.69 W/m², still below 40.1 W/m². The majority of the gap arises on the thermal side: the 7-layer design achieves an average 8–13 µm window emissivity of 0.386 in our simulator (using Franta database optical constants), while the analytic clear-sky model radiates P_atm = 84.57 W/m² back down onto the surface.

search_space.layer_order: materials[0] faces the sky; materials[-1] touches the substrate

evaluation_unit: one simulate_stack call (counted inside lab.physics, invalid designs included)
